description: Columbia University provides SEDAT desalination technology models and a graphical application for examining solar-powered water supply. The application offers interactive site selection and solar, desalination and financial model choices. Its own repository lists multi-effect distillation variants, membrane distillation, reverse osmosis, forward osmosis and hybrid configurations. The README directs users to a complete Google Drive application package because the larger data files are not stored in GitHub; the repository contains code and smaller inputs. Access is public and free. The describing paper states Academic Free License for the code, but gives no version, and the current repository has no identified licence file. Geographic coverage follows the selected GIS and energy inputs, not a fixed site. The tool can support capacity and technology-comparison simulations alongside model-watertap and data-nsrdb-national-solar-radiation-database. A caveat is that the GitHub checkout alone is not documented as the complete runnable application. Current package availability, dependencies and licence details need checking before deployment. No full application archive was downloaded or executed.
